# Results — Study 504 (Coskewness): does the crash-sensitive tail pay a premium?

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Harvey-Siddique (2000)
**coskewness** sort — each month, measure every name's **direct standardised coskewness** with
the market over the trailing 12 months (``E[e_i·e_m²] / (√E[e_i²]·E[e_m²])`` on demeaned daily
returns), form quintiles, and go **long the low-coskewness names, short the high-coskewness
ones** — tested on a **transparent large-cap proxy**. Coskewness is a *systematic*,
undiversifiable tail measure (a name's contribution to the **market's** skewness), the opposite
axis from the *idiosyncratic* tail of [Study 503](../503-expected-idiosyncratic-skewness/). True
coskewness pricing is a CRSP-universe object; yfinance gives only a large-cap slice, so we run the
sort on a fixed **S&P-100-style basket** and call it a proxy throughout. Offline core + synthetic
control are deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Coskewness premium?" `BUSTED`

Harvey-Siddique says a name's *systematic* tail — how hard it falls when the market falls hard —
is priced: **low (negative) coskewness** is a bad hedge, so it should pay a **premium**. On this
large-cap survivor proxy the tilt is in the **right direction but tiny and insignificant**: the
low-coskew quintile (Q1) returned **+15.2%/yr** and the high-coskew quintile (Q5) **+13.9%/yr**,
so the textbook long-low / short-high book earns a gross **+1.3%/yr** at HAC **t = +0.40** —
indistinguishable from a coin (49% win-rate, placebo *p* = 0.35). The spread stays near zero
across tertile / quintile / decile cuts (deciles reach only *t* = 0.62) and in both halves of the
sample; it never clears *t* = 2. The published cross-sectional premium is small even in the full
CRSP universe; on liquid, surviving large-caps it shrinks into the noise. `NONE` on Signal (the
premium has the right sign but is statistically absent, and the basket is **survivorship**-tilted
— named on the axis), `MIRAGE` on Tradability (the +1.3%/yr gross is far too small to survive
costs — 20 bps/leg + borrow turn it into a −4.0%/yr loss), and `BUSTED` on the folklore (a
real-money coskewness premium does **not** emerge on the names large-cap investors hold).

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — a fixed **S&P-100-style 79-name large-cap basket + SPY** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**5,385** trading days; **21.4** years; partial 2026-06 bar dropped) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (last complete month-end); inputs fingerprint `abdf2637ac09` |
| Signal | **coskewness** = Harvey-Siddique direct standardised coskewness ``E[e_i·e_m²]/(√E[e_i²]·E[e_m²])`` of daily returns vs market (SPY) over the trailing 12 months, per name, at month-end |
| Sort | rank cross-section by coskewness → quintiles Q1 (low / negative) … Q5 (high); equal-weight next-month return |
| Trade | long Q1 (low-coskew) / short Q5 (high-coskew), monthly; monthly signal ⇒ full monthly turnover |
| Costs | 20 bps one-way per leg × turnover + 50 bps/yr short borrow on the high-coskew leg |

> **Proxy + survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** A fixed ~79-name surviving
> large-cap basket is a thin, high-quality slice of the market — not the broad CRSP cross-section
> Harvey-Siddique priced. Coskewness is best identified where the dispersion in crash-sensitivity
> is widest (smaller, more cyclical, more leveraged names); a basket of mega-cap survivors
> compresses that dispersion and survivorship trims the very names whose low-coskew risk
> *materialised* (the ones that fell hardest and de-listed). Both forces push the measured premium
> *toward zero* here, and we say so: this tape shows the published premium **does not survive** the
> large-cap, survivor universe — it cannot certify the CRSP result either way. **Opt-in guard:**
> widen to a few-thousand-name panel including de-listed names (paid, point-in-time feed) to test
> the premium in its native habitat.

## The cross-section — flat, with the faintest correct tilt

251 monthly cross-sections (2005-06 → 2026-04). Each quintile's next-month return,
equal-weighted, annualised:

| quintile | coskewness rank | mean / yr | vol | Sharpe |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 | **lowest** coskew (crash-sensitive) | **+15.2%** | 19.3% | 0.79 |
| Q2 | | +15.4% | 16.3% | 0.94 |
| Q3 | | +15.9% | 15.6% | **1.02** |
| Q4 | | +15.2% | 15.4% | 0.99 |
| Q5 | **highest** coskew (insurance-like) | **+13.9%** | 15.5% | 0.90 |

The risk story predicts Q1 ≫ Q5. The line is essentially **flat**: Q1 (+15.2%/yr) edges Q5
(+13.9%/yr) by a hair in the *right* direction, but the peak return is the *middle* bucket (Q3,
+15.9%) — no monotone slope, and Q1 carries the **highest vol** (19.3%), so its Sharpe is the
*worst* of the five. The crash-sensitive leg earns a faint extra return and a *lot* of extra
risk — the very definition of an unrewarded tilt.

## The trade — long low-coskew / short high-coskew is a coin gross, a loser net

| book | mean / yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* | win-rate | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 − Q5 (long low-coskew, short high-coskew), **gross** | **+1.3%** | +0.08 | **+0.40** | 49% | 0.352 |
| Q1 − Q5, **net** (20 bps/leg + 50 bps/yr borrow) | −4.0% | −0.25 | **−1.24** | 42% | — |

Gross, the textbook trade is **indistinguishable from zero** (HAC *t* = +0.40, placebo
*p* = 0.35, a coin-flip 49% win-rate) — the premium has the right *sign* but no statistical
weight. The *net* book is negative (*t* = −1.24, still inside the bar): a +1.3%/yr gross edge is
far too thin to pay 2 × 20 bps/leg plus borrow on a full-turnover monthly book. There is no edge
large enough to deploy. `REAL` requires *t* ≥ 2 **gross, in the claimed direction**; this is
*t* = +0.40.

## Robustness — flat everywhere, never significant

| cut | n | mean / yr (low − high) | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| tertiles (Q1 − Q3) | 251 | −0.0% | −0.00 | 49% |
| **quintiles (Q1 − Q5)** | 251 | **+1.3%** | **+0.40** | 49% |
| deciles (Q1 − Q10) | 251 | +2.5% | +0.62 | 54% |

Cutting harder into the tails nudges the spread up a touch (deciles +2.5%/yr) but only to
*t* = 0.62 — never near significance. The faint right-direction tilt grows with the cut but stays
deep inside the noise.

| sub-period | n | mean / yr | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005–2015 | 127 | +1.9% | +0.40 |
| 2016–2026 | 124 | +0.7% | +0.17 |

Near zero in **both** halves — the (correct-signed) premium is faintly present throughout, never
significant in either window.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful (and seed-robust)

A deterministic monthly panel with a **planted coskewness premium** (low-coskew names made to
out-perform next month by ``edge`` × standardised −coskewness) confirms the sort + inference
recover a *real* low-minus-high premium when one is present, and find **nothing** when it is
absent. Per the house bar, the control's *t* is averaged over **20 seeds**:

| planted edge | Q1 − Q5 mean / yr | HAC *t* (seed 504) | seed-robust mean *t* (20 seeds) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.000** (no edge) | +0.1% | +0.05 | **+0.24** (sd 1.08) |
| **+0.004** (real coskew premium) | +13.4% | +7.60 | **+8.58** (sd 1.28) |

With **no** planted edge the harness sits near *t* = 0 across seeds (no false positive); with a
modest planted premium it turns the spread cleanly positive at mean *t* = +8.58 over 20 seeds.
So the machinery is honest: the **flat** *t* on the real tape is a genuine feature of the
large-cap survivor cross-section, not a coding artefact, and a *real* coskewness premium of any
useful size would have shown up as a clean **positive** spread had one existed here.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed low-coskew premium is **statistically absent** on this tape; the
  gross long-low / short-high spread is **+1.3%/yr at HAC *t* = +0.40** (placebo *p* = 0.35) — a
  coin, even though the sign is the right one. The result is flat across cut granularity and both
  sub-periods, and the universe is a **survivorship**-tilted large-cap proxy (named on the Signal
  axis). The published CRSP cross-sectional premium is not reproduced — and cannot be certified —
  on a surviving large-cap universe.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A +1.3%/yr gross edge is far too thin to deploy; net of 20 bps/leg +
  50 bps/yr borrow on a full-turnover monthly book it is **−4.0%/yr (*t* = −1.24)** — the
  frictions swallow the whole (insignificant) premium. Nothing here to allocate to.
- **"Coskewness premium"? — BUSTED.** On liquid, surviving large-caps the crash-sensitive
  (low-coskew) tail did **not** pay a usable premium — it edged the insurance-like tail by a hair
  while carrying the **highest** volatility of the five buckets (worst Sharpe). The systematic-skew
  premium is a broad-universe, dispersion-rich phenomenon that compresses to noise among the
  mega-cap survivors most investors actually hold.
